subject: [PATCH] memcg: flush nr_charged_bytes when the obj stock trylock fails

reviews.author: Muchun Song
reviews.summary: Acked the patch without providing any specific feedback or concerns.
reviews.raw_body:
> On Nov 12, 2026, at 09:32, Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev> wrote:
> 
> When interrupt code, such as an RCU callback in softirq, runs on top of
> a task that holds the obj stock lock, its trylock fails and the bytes go
> to objcg->nr_charged_bytes. Nothing empties that counter while every CPU
> using the objcg keeps it in its stock, so it can grow without limit.
> 
> Users see memory.current and the "kernel" field of memory.stat keep
> growing while the cgroup's real usage does not. With memory.high or
> memory.max set, the cgroup is reclaimed, throttled or even OOM-killed
> for memory it does not use. The counter is 32-bit, so after 4 GiB it
> wraps, and those 4 GiB stay charged to the cgroup and its ancestors
> until reboot, even after the cgroup is removed.
> 
> Fix it by uncharging the whole pages in nr_charged_bytes whenever the
> trylock fails.
> 
> Fixes: 200577f69f29 ("memcg: objcg stock trylock without irq disabling")
> Reported-by: Chris Mason <mason@kernel.org>
> Signed-off-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

Acked-by: Muchun Song (ByteDance) <muchun.song@linux.dev>

Thanks.

reviews.author: Vlastimil Babka
reviews.summary: Also acked the patch without raising any specific issues or concerns.

reviews.author: Harry Yoo

reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 05:32:20PM -0800, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> When interrupt code, such as an RCU callback in softirq, runs on top of

> using the objcg keeps it in its stock, so it can grow without limit.
> 
> Users see memory.current and the "kernel" field of memory.stat keep
> growing while the cgroup's real usage does not. With memory.high or
> memory.max set, the cgroup is reclaimed, throttled or even OOM-killed
> for memory it does not use. The counter is 32-bit, so after 4 GiB it
> wraps, and those 4 GiB stay charged to the cgroup and its ancestors
> until reboot, even after the cgroup is removed.
> 
> Fix it by uncharging the whole pages in nr_charged_bytes whenever the
> trylock fails.
> 
> Fixes: 200577f69f29 ("memcg: objcg stock trylock without irq disabling")

Looks good to me,
Reviewed-by: Harry Yoo (Meta) <harry@kernel.org>

>  mm/memcontrol.c | 2 ++
>  1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)
> 
> diff --git a/mm/memcontrol.c b/mm/memcontrol.c
> index f5f567f7d4a9..091401cecf39 100644
> --- a/mm/memcontrol.c
> +++ b/mm/memcontrol.c
> @@ -3553,6 +3553,8 @@ static void __refill_obj_stock(struct obj_cgroup *objcg,
>  	int i, slot = -1, empty_slot = -1;
>  
>  	if (!stock) {
> +		nr_bytes += atomic_read(&objcg->nr_charged_bytes)
> +			? atomic_xchg(&objcg->nr_charged_bytes, 0) : 0;
>  		nr_pages = nr_bytes >> PAGE_SHIFT;
>  		nr_bytes = nr_bytes & (PAGE_SIZE - 1);
>  		atomic_add(nr_bytes, &objcg->nr_charged_bytes);
> -- 
> 2.53.0-Meta

-- 
Cheers,
Harry / Hyeonggon

2026-11-12.patch_summary: The patch addresses a memory accounting issue in the Linux kernel's memcg (memory cgroup) subsystem, where the nr_charged_bytes counter can grow indefinitely when an interrupt handler tries to acquire the obj stock lock and fails. This causes incorrect memory usage reports for tasks within the affected cgroups. The fix involves uncharging the pages stored in nr_charged_bytes whenever the trylock fails.
